turns.question: Where is application-level route handling wired up, and is the router itself implemented inside this repository?
turns.text:
I'll inspect the expressjs/express repo structure and key files via GitHub API without cloning.I have everything needed to answer confidently.

## Where application-level route handling is wired up

**File: `lib/express.js`**
- Requires the router package: `var Router = require('router');` and re-exports it: `exports.Route = Router.Route; exports.Router = Router;`
- Builds the app object (a callable function) and mixes in `application.js`'s prototype (`proto`) via `merge-descriptors`.

**File: `lib/application.js`** — this is the actual wiring layer:
- `app.init()` (around line 60-82) lazily creates the app's root router instance: `router = new Router({ caseSensitive: ..., strict: ... })`, exposed via a getter property `this.router`.
- `app.handle()` (~line 177) delegates every incoming request to it: `this.router.handle(req, res, done)`.
- `app.use()` (~line 195-245) is a documented proxy: *"Proxy `Router#use()` to add middleware to the app router"* — it grabs `this.router` and calls `router.use(path, fn)`, with special-case handling for mounting sub-apps (`mounted_app` wrapper that restores `req.app`/`res.app` prototypes).
- `app.route()` (~line 257) is *"Proxy to the app `Router#route()`"* — returns `this.router.route(path)`.
- `app.param()` (~line 331) proxies to `this.router.param(name, fn)`.
- The `methods.forEach(...)` block (~line 468) delegates `app.get/post/put/...()` calls to `this.route(path)[method](...)`.

So application.js is a thin façade: it doesn't implement routing logic itself, it lazily instantiates one `Router` per app and forwards `use`, `route`, `param`, and verb methods to it, plus handles Express-specific concerns (mounting sub-apps, settings inheritance, view rendering, etc.).

## Is the router implemented inside this repo?

**No.** In current Express (v5.2.1, confirmed via `package.json`), the router is an external dependency:
```json
"router": "^2.2.0"
```
and `lib/express.js` / `lib/application.js` simply `require('router')`. There is no `lib/router/` directory in this repo — I confirmed `gh api repos/expressjs/express/contents/lib/router` returns `404 Not Found`. `lib/` only contains `application.js`, `express.js`, `request.js`, `response.js`, `utils.js`, `view.js`.

The actual `Router`, `Route`, and layer-matching logic live in the separate package **pillarjs/router** (`https://github.com/pillarjs/router`, described as "Simple middleware-style router"), pulled in as a normal npm dependency.

Note: this is a change from Express 4.x, where the router (`lib/router/index.js`, `lib/router/route.js`, `lib/router/layer.js`) was implemented in-tree. Express 5 extracted it into the standalone `router` package.

## What I did not verify
- I didn't clone/diff pillarjs/router's source itself, so I can't describe its internal matching algorithm (path-to-regexp version, layer/route internals) — only that Express's app layer treats it as an opaque dependency.
- I didn't check every Express 4.x tag to pinpoint exactly which release removed `lib/router/`; I'm relying on the current `package.json` dependency and the 404 on `lib/router` as evidence for the present state only.
- I read `application.js` via `sed` excerpts, not the full file end-to-end, so there could be other minor router-touching methods I didn't quote (though the pattern is consistent throughout: proxy to `this.router`).

# Unreleased Changes

## 🐞 Bug fixes

- Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by [@YuryShkoda](https://github.com/YuryShkoda) in [#4893](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/4893)


    Fixed the behavior of `res.send()` to prevent conflicts between `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` HTTP headers in responses. The `Content-Length` header in `res.send()` is now only added when a `Transfer-Encoding` header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response

## 🚀 Improvements

* Improve HTML structure in `res.redirect()` responses when HTML format is accepted by adding `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<title>`, and `<body>` tags for better browser compatibility - by [@Bernice55231](https://github.com/Bernice55231) in [#5167](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/5167)

* When calling `app.render` with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by [AkaHarshit](https://github.com/AkaHarshit) in [#6903](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6903)

    ```js
    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected
    ```

* Upgrade `content-type` to `^2.0.0`, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker `Content-Type` parsing/formatting in `res.send()`) along with a behavior change: `res.send()` now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a `Content-Type` that fails to parse - by [@blakeembrey](https://github.com/blakeembrey) in [#7234](https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7234)

    ```js
    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
    // -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; c
